answer: Each agent locks a 60-credit bond and registers one device before a voyage. It counts only if that device is sighted at a grove waypoint and then a ledge checkpoint in one ten-minute window, both signed by two witnesses. The first fake identity costs 70 in fees; the k-th costs 70+10(k-1), since each simultaneous identity needs its own device at once, so the 1000th costs 10,060, and 1000 fakes cost 5,065,000 plus 60,000 locked. An honest agent pays once. A rented-device ring fails: one device cannot sign two identities in one window, and duplicate serials slash the group.
